decisions.reason: 2.1 draws every chained head in the hold turned to the musket, with Nagoji's pen placed a few yards behind it. Keshavrao shares that pen: he is beside Nagoji in 1.2, 2.3 and 3.3, and in 2.3 his eyes are on the musket. If Nagoji counts as drawn in that pen, Keshavrao does too. The draft's nagoji-only cast came from name matching, not from the art.

The 2.3 insert describes only Nagoji's left hand, sleeve and branded forearm "on the reins of the grey"; the reins are tack, and no part of the horse (neck, mane, head) is described, so grey_gelding is not drawn.

7.2 draws Raza Khan rising and Nagoji "already walking back toward his grey"; the grey is only where he is heading and gets no description or placement in the frame, so listing grey_gelding would be a guess.

9.2 draws only Padmini Amma's stick pointing past Nagoji's shoulder, with no arm, hand or 'at the edge of frame' (6.2 and 9.3 do say that). A prop alone is not a body part, and a missing '(off)' tag does not make her drawn, so this matches 5.3, where she is left out.

The art line "Revathi's eyes finding Nagoji's" draws only Revathi; Nagoji is just who she is looking at and is never placed in frame (compare 8.5 and 3.6 in the same script). He is first staged in 13.3 ("Nagoji beside her").

The art describes only Revathi (wiped cheeks, smile, stepping close); "him" is only a reference point, like "toward him" in ch24 2.2 and "facing him fully" in ch27 6.5. Nagoji is explicitly drawn in the next panel, 14.6 ("her face at Nagoji's ear").

Nagoji is drawn watching Varma leave. He is mounted in 10.1 ('rides up') and in 10.5 ('on Kayal'), with no dismount in between, so Kayal is drawn under him in 10.4. This matches the neighbour inference the draft already used for 5.5 and 10.1. Varma's own horse is unnamed and is not a key.

14.3 draws only the falling-out men grinning up at Nagoji in his foreign cloth; no horse is described, and the script's continuity block lists Megha only at 12.2 and 14.2, so the mount is implied by 'grinning up' but not drawn.

Nagoji crawls in the foreground. Varma is drawn as the large shadow on the wall, kneeling with one hand fisted in the chaver's hair, and that shadow stages the panel's action. The rules count a silhouette and even indirect 'stain' images, so this counts too. The note about infer_cast only concerns attaching his face sheet, not whether he is drawn.

The art description draws 'Madurai lancers with tall spears' in Nagoji's column, with him at its head on Kayal. The ch12 notes call Raza Khan's Madurai lancers Travancore's standing cavalry, and the pipeline maps 'madurai lancers' to this key. Nothing in the ch22 script sets them apart as a separate group.

The 10.5 art line says Ponnan is "still gripping the wrist". The panel can only show that if the grip, and so Nagoji's sword wrist from 10.3 and 10.4, is in frame. That wrist is an identifiable body part, the same one that puts Nagoji in the 10.3 insert.

The art note only names Thoma, but this script tags every off-panel Nagoji line '(off)' (10.1, 11.x, 16.4, 19.x, 26.3). His line here has no tag, he is watching Thoma at the gun in 27.1 and standing beside him in 27.5, and CHAPTER-24-CAST-OVERRIDES.json sets this panel to [nagoji, thoma] while leaving 27.2 and 27.4 as [thoma]. Nagoji is drawn.

It follows 30.1, 'Two men in the lamplight'. De Lannoy smiles 'at Nagoji's answer', Nagoji's line has no '(off)' tag, and the overrides file sets this panel to [eustachius, nagoji]. Both men are drawn.

De Lannoy is 'staring at some point between them', which puts both men in the frame. Nagoji's question has no '(off)' tag, both men are drawn in 29.1 and 29.2, and 29.5 has De Lannoy 'turned back to Nagoji'. There is no override for this panel, and the pipeline's own inference would add nagoji anyway.

The woman's hands come from the novel's line 'My mother tying a charm on my wrist' (ch25 source, line 130), which the adaptation note says the four-fragment montage keeps. So they are Nagoji's mother's hands, drawn, on the same footing as Keshavrao's hand-only fragment. Nagoji is drawn writing, Padmini's face is shown, and the spyglass boy is an unnamed lookout.

This script marks every off-panel speaker with (off) (3.2, 3.4, 5.2, 10.2-10.4, 11.2, 11.3, 12.5), and Nagoji's two balloons in 11.4 are unmarked. That puts him in frame across from Ramayyan, which matches the draft's own reading of 7.1 and the two-man staging of 11.5.

1.5 draws 'the men around her', blurred, and rule 1 counts blurred or silhouette figures as drawn; in 1.3 and 3.1 the only men around her at the map table are Ramayyan across it, Varma on the platform behind and Nagoji by the pillar, so they are identified by rule 3, while the runner in the doorway is an unnamed extra.

'The priests intone' is part of the 5.5 art description, not just the lettering. The PRIESTS balloon has no (off) tag, and this script marks off-panel speakers with (off), as it does for Revathi and Nagoji on pages 6-7. The shot looks toward the sanctum threshold, where 2.1 puts the row of Hindu temple priests (drawn again in 3.3), so they are in frame behind Varma. The whispering chief is not a key and Nagoji is not drawn.
